digest.component_or_area: ticket store rewrite and epoch migration
propositions: Execute a one-time destructive rewrite of the tickets branch (force-with-lease after A5, A6-0a through A6-0d, and Epic B's B6 closure) to reclaim 92% of storage by deleting the epoch-blind writer era history, guarded by pre-publication assertions and operator-confirmed writer quiescence
Disable all continuous reconciliation workflows and verify zero in-flight sessions via review-bot /health, Gerrit open-patchset queries, and explicit MCP server shutdown before beginning the rewrite
Refresh and probe the host rebar runtime and deployed review-bot against a temporary clone to confirm epoch-mismatch refusal works before publication, replacing the former 24-hour elapsed-time proxy

Perform the history strip in a fresh unfiltered clone, verify tree equality and commit/merge counts, assert non-resurrection via git merge-base and default-clone ref inspection, and confirm <1 MB pack growth after the first post-window write
Converge the local tracker and review-bot clone to the rewritten history via direct fetch+reset and SSM send-command, then re-pin identity.enforce_since through normal Gerrit review/submit

After re-enable, validate post-window reconciliation (green reconcile-bridge.yml run or operator-approved CLI sequence with zero mutation/recovery failures and canary drift_total=0) and confirm rebar fsck is clean with exactly the four intentional fork-resolved audit records
